---
title: "Assignments"
toc: false   # hub page, keep the full content width, unlike the assignments themselves
---

Every assignment arrives as **your own private GitHub repository**, created for you inside the course organization. Clone it and work in VS Code.

Your repository is checked automatically each time you push, and the tests tell you how you are doing. **That score does not set your grade**, assignments count as *complete* when you submit reasonable work, green tests or not. See [Grading](../../policies/grading.html) for how completion feeds into your final grade.

Before any of this can happen, you must send your GitHub username to your instructor and accept the invitation to the course organization, [Getting Started](gettingStarted.html) walks you through it.

Assignments are grouped by the week they begin. Weeks carrying **more than one** assignment are marked with a heavier rule and a bold count, plan ahead for those.

Each assignment **opens on the Monday of its week**. You can see the whole term below, but a future assignment stays grayed out with its opening date until then.

::: {.callout-tip}
Each assignment page lists the **skills** it gives you evidence for. If your submitted work clearly demonstrates a skill, you don't need a check-in appointment for it, see [Skills & Check-Ins](../checkins.html).
:::
